chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Bajali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Love the children and be merciful to them, and when you promise them something, fulfill it for them, for they do not know except that you are sustaining them.'

key_terms.فَفُوا لَهُمْ: fulfill it for them (from the verb to fulfill a promise)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about how parents should treat their children?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet’s (SAWW) emphasis on treating children with tenderness and integrity, noting that their limited cognitive understanding makes them view adults solely as providers. This teaching underscores the spiritual weight of even minor promises, fostering a foundation of trust (amanah) and emotional security essential for their moral development. It reflects the Shia focus on nurturing the child’s heart through consistent, loving action rather than mere authority.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Bajaly, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Love your children and be merciful to them, and when you promise them something, so fulfill it for them, for they do not know except that you are sustaining them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Bajaliy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
You must love children and be kind to them. If you promise them, then keep your promise because they do not know anyone except you who provides them sustenance.’”
